_comment: Unwrap() count ratchet (issue #706). Counts are OCCURRENCES of `.unwrap()` and must never increase. Update downward as unwraps are removed.
_baseline_policy: These numbers are a DELIBERATE ACCEPTANCE, not a measurement to be refreshed. Raising one is a decision that needs a reason recorded in this file and a reviewer who agrees with it. There is deliberately NO regenerate script: a ratchet whose baseline can be widened by running a command is not a ratchet, because the same PR that adds an unwrap could silence the gate that caught it.
_rebaselined_2026_07_22: Raised from 180/159 to the counts on main at fea3500c7, implementing the decision recorded on #2269. Rationale: the gate had been failing on every Rust PR for reasons unrelated to that PR, which is how a gate stops being read. WHAT THIS NOW TOLERATES: 620 occurrences, of which all but 2 sit inside #[cfg(test)] modules; the 2 production ones are shared-protocol/src/consensus/proof_of_publishing.rs:3780 and shared-protocol/src/blockchain/chain.rs:426, each guarded by a preceding check. WHAT IT PREVENTS: any increase at all, in test and production code alike.
_counts_occurrences_not_lines: Review of #2278 found the gate counted matching LINES (`grep ... | wc -l`), so a second `.unwrap()` added to an already-counted line left the total unchanged and passed. It now counts occurrences, so the same-line case fails. This is the #2284 class: a gate measured at a coarser granularity than the violation it detects.
_production_scope_2026_07_22: Re-measured 297/323 -> 1/1 when the counter changed from raw text-matching (scripts/count_unwraps.py replaces `grep -ro`) to production-scope counting: comments, string literals, doc examples, and #[cfg(test)]/#[test] code no longer count (second #2278 review). The code did not change — the metric did. The two remaining production occurrences are exactly the two the previous rebaseline note already named as deliberate acceptances: shared-protocol/src/consensus/proof_of_publishing.rs:3780 and shared-protocol/src/blockchain/chain.rs:426, each guarded by a preceding check. The counter's own regression suite (scripts/test_count_unwraps.py) runs in the ratchet step before every comparison.
